I gave GPT-6 Astra the Zillow listing for this house and said I wanted to generate a 30 second walkthrough with a real estate agent. 

I asked it pick images to use, write a prompt w/ time stamps, and ensure the audio hit the right parts of the walkthrough. 

Final prompt:

Create a photorealistic, approximately 30-second real estate tour of 146 Lenox Way, San Francisco, in vertical 9:16. 

VISUAL APPROACH 
Film this as a real camera accompanying a realtor inside the actual property. Each reference photograph establishes the appearance of its location.  The presenter must inhabit the room at believable human scale, with perspective, lighting, shadows, and focus consistent with her surroundings. Position her on the actual floor beside recognizable furniture or architectural features. Where appropriate, nearby furniture should naturally overlap part of her lower body to establish depth.  Use an eye-level camera. In presenter shots, frame her approximately mid-thigh upward, with her eyes near the upper third of the screen. Keep her head comfortably below the top edge. Balance her with the feature she describes.  Avoid the appearance of a small presenter placed along the bottom of a background image. Avoid excessive empty ceiling, sky, or floor.  Use subtle, physical camera movement: a short sideways track or gentle movement toward the presenter, with natural changes in perspective between foreground and background. Do not animate the reference photographs as slides or use digital zooms on still images.  Preserve the property’s visible architecture, finishes, furniture, and room proportions. Select a believable vertical camera composition without stretching the room or inventing additional space. 

 PRESENTER AND SOUND 
Use the same young adult Asian female realtor throughout: natural appearance, dark hair, beige suit, white top. Maintain her identity, clothing, and conversational voice.  

She appears and speaks with accurate lip-sync in shots 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7. SHOT 5 IS THE EXCEPTION: show only the bedroom and bathroom interiors. The realtor continues speaking as voiceover. No person appears in these three interior views.  Use only the exact dialogue below. No music or added dialogue. Let each sentence finish before the next spoken line begins.  

SHOT 1 — EXTERIOR — approximately 0:00–0:07 
Use IMAGE 1 as reference. The realtor stands beside the front steps, correctly scaled to the railing and entrance. Frame her mid-thigh upward, eyes near the upper third, with the recognizable facade behind her. She welcomes the viewer with a small natural gesture. The camera gently approaches.  She says: “Welcome to 146 Lenox Way—fourteen hundred square feet of West Portal charm.”  Pronounce 146 as “one forty-six.”  

SHOT 2 — LIVING ROOM — approximately 0:07–0:11 
Use Image 2 as reference. The realtor stands beside the seating area, physically within the room. Frame her and the built-ins together. She turns slightly toward the built-ins, gestures, and looks back to camera. Make a short sideways camera move. She says: “The living room features beautiful custom built-ins…”  

SHOT 3 — DINING ROOM — approximately 0:11–0:14 
Use Image 3 as reference. The realtor stands beside the dining table at believable scale. The table edge occupies part of the foreground, establishing depth. She addresses the camera as it moves gently sideways. She says: “…and opens into a formal dining room.” 

 SHOT 4 — KITCHEN — approximately 0:14–0:17 
Use Image 4 as reference. Place the realtor in the existing open floor area beside the counter. Frame her upper body and the kitchen together. She gestures naturally toward the kitchen. Preserve the actual layout; do not merge separate reference photographs into a fabricated room. She says: “The kitchen has a breakfast nook nearby.”  

SHOT 5 — BEDROOM AND BATHROOM CUTAWAYS — approximately 0:17–0:21
Use Image 5, 6, and 7 as reference. Show each space without any presenter or other person. Use three brief, cleanly cut interior views with subtle camera movement. Preserve each room’s separate identity and layout. No dissolves or transformations between rooms. The realtor’s same voice continues OFF CAMERA: “Three bedrooms and two baths, all on one level.”  

SHOT 6 — DOWNSTAIRS FLEX ROOM — approximately 0:21–0:25
Use Image 7 as reference. The realtor returns on camera, standing beside the seating area at realistic scale. Frame her mid-thigh upward. Preserve the actual ceiling height and exposed features. Make a gentle sideways camera move; do not invent a garage view. She says: “Downstairs, a two-car garage and flexible bonus space.”  

SHOT 7 — BACKYARD — approximately 0:25–0:30 
Use Image 8 as reference. The realtor stands on the paved area with the garden behind her. Frame her mid-thigh upward, eyes near the upper third. She gestures toward the yard, then addresses the viewer directly as the camera gently approaches. She says: “A flat, fenced backyard for entertaining. Come tour today!” Finish on her natural smile in the backyard.
